claims.explanation: Torin-1 is a dual mTORC1/mTORC2 ATP-competitive inhibitor, so selectivity likely reflects dependence on mTOR-driven cap-dependent translation and growth signaling, especially in lines with activated PI3K/AKT/mTOR or receptor tyrosine kinase/MAPK inputs. Lines with PIK3CA, PTEN, EGFR, MET, BRAF, or NF1 alterations are enriched among sensitive lines, whereas several resistant lines have RAS/RAF alterations without upstream PI3K pathway activation or are neuroblastoma/mesothelioma lines with low mTOR dependence. High mTOR pathway activity and high expression of mTOR/translation-related genes should therefore predict sensitivity.

features.basis: Activating PI3K mutations enrich in sensitive lines and increase mTORC1 dependence
PTEN loss hyperactivates PI3K/AKT/mTOR and is seen in sensitive lines
Higher mTOR expression/activity increases dependence on the drug target
EGFR-driven lines are enriched among sensitive lines and signal through mTOR
MET alterations appear in sensitive lines and activate PI3K/mTOR
BRAF-mutant melanoma/thyroid lines are among sensitive lines via MAPK-mTOR crosstalk
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and can increase mTOR pathway output
TOR/S6K1-eIF3h-dependent translation reinitiation is inhibited by Torin-1
S6K1 is a key mTORC1 effector whose activity is blocked by Torin-1
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among least affected lines, suggesting MAPK-driven mTOR independence
NRAS-mutant melanoma/neuroblastoma lines appear resistant to Torin-1
ALK-altered neuroblastoma lines are among the least affected lines
